extracted.intended_audience: independent inventors and small-business inventors preparing US utility patent applications
extracted.subtask_short: preparing a US utility patent application
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, step-by-step guidance for inventors on what a US utility patent covers, the statutory patentability requirements, documentation and search practices, application components, prosecution, fees, and international filing options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of a utility patent (what it covers)
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility patent protects new, useful, and non-obvious processes, machines, manufactures, and compositions of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent gives the owner the right to exclude others from making, using, selling, offering to sell, or importing the patented invention for 20 years from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject matter (35 U.S.C. §101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter (35 USC 101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excludes laws of nature, natural phenomena, and abstract ideas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must have a practical use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty requirement (35 U.S.C. §102)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not anticipated by a single piece of prior art (35 USC 102).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-obviousness requirement (35 U.S.C. §103)
rubrics_metrics.description: Not obvious to a person of ordinary skill in the art (35 USC 103).

rubrics_metrics.name: Document the invention early (inventor's notebook)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain a dated, signed inventor's notebook. Record the conception of the invention, reductions to practice, and steps taken to develop the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the AIA moved the US to first-to-file, documentation still helps establish inventorship and supports prior-user-rights defenses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art search before filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Search the USPTO patent database, Google Patents, foreign patent databases (Espacenet, J-PlatPat, KIPRIS), and academic literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The search informs what is novel and what claim scope is realistic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and limits of provisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional application is a 12-month placeholder. It is not examined and never matures into a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 12 months can be used to refine the invention, raise funding, or test the market. The non-provisional must be filed within 12 months and only gets priority for what is actually disclosed in the provisional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-provisional application components
rubrics_metrics.description: Required parts of a non-provisional application include: Title; Abstract; Background; Summary; Brief Description of Drawings; Detailed Description; Claims; Drawings; Oath/Declaration; Information Disclosure Statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each component plays a role in disclosure and claim support (claims define the invention; the detailed description and drawings support the claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing fees and entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees vary by entity status: micro, small, large.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For small entity (most individuals and small businesses) approximate amounts given: Filing fee ~$80; Search fee ~$370; Examination fee ~$430; Issue fee ~$600; Maintenance fees ~$800 / $1,800 / $3,700 at 3.5/7.5/11.5 years. Large entity fees are double; micro entity is half of small entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent prosecution process expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: After filing, an examiner reviews the application. Most applications receive at least one office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant responds with arguments and/or amendments. The process continues until allowance or final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to hire a patent attorney or agent
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent law is highly specialized; consider hiring counsel licensed to the patent bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent attorneys (J.D. plus admission to the patent bar) and patent agents (technical degree plus admission to the patent bar) are licensed by the USPTO to draft and prosecute patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-issuance requirements and rights
rubrics_metrics.description: After the patent issues, maintenance fees must be paid to keep the patent in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner can sue for infringement, license the patent, or sell it. Patent rights are territorial; US patents do not protect outside the US.

rubrics_metrics.name: International protection and timing (priority claims and PCT)
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 12 months of US filing, the inventor can file in other countries claiming priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PCT route delays the country-by-country decision by 30 months from priority.
